blocks.text: AI Creative Media Academy teaches students to direct AI instead of being replaced by it. Students turn their own idea into a short vertical video, learning how to write prompts, direct voice, create visuals, animate images, and edit, while thinking carefully about honesty, privacy, and responsible use.

rows: Beginner, no prior AI experience needed

blocks.text: Main learning flow: IDEA → STORY → VOICE → SCENE → IMAGE → VIDEO → EDIT → SHARE.

items: Explain what AI is, what it can do, and its limits, including that AI can be wrong or biased.
Write clear prompts with context, goal, and instructions.
Write a short story script with a beginning, middle, and ending.
Direct a voice-over through character, emotion, and pacing.
Plan scenes with a storyboard and keep visuals consistent.
Turn images into short videos with motion and transitions.
Edit audio, subtitles, and thumbnail, and present the work.
Use AI honestly, safely, and with credit.
ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini: ideas, scripts, prompts, and feedback.
Image generator and image-to-video tools such as Dola and Dreamina (teacher-guided).
Canva: editing, subtitles, thumbnail, and presentation.
Generating is done with school or teacher accounts, following each platform's age rules; students do not need personal AI accounts.
No personal data, face photos, full names, voices, or family information goes into public AI tools.
Student work is shared only after teacher and, when needed, parent approval.
Students always check AI answers and credit AI help.
One vertical 9:16 video of about 20–40 seconds with 4–6 short scenes.
A narrator or two characters, consistent visuals, simple transitions, and subtitles.
A thumbnail, a caption, and the statement: “Made with AI assistance and the student's creative decisions.”

blocks.text: Learning outcome: Students explain what AI can and cannot do, and agree on rules for using it honestly and safely.

rows: Teacher demo: How AI works in simple terms, with examples of good and wrong AI answers.
Guided practice: Sort examples into human idea, human decision, and AI help.
Creative production: Write a personal AI Promise: safe, honest, responsible.
Reflection & saving files: Share one rule; create a personal project folder.

blocks.text: AI Promise card and project folder.
Learning outcome: Students choose a useful story idea and write a short script with a hook, middle, and closing.

rows: Opening: Spark ideas from safe themes: kindness, environment, school life, local culture.
Teacher demo: Turn one broad topic into a short video idea and a 5–7 sentence script.
Guided practice: Co-write a sample script with an AI assistant and edit it together.
Creative production: Write and improve a personal script for a 20–40 second video.
Reflection & saving files: Read the script aloud; mark parts that are too long or unclear.

blocks.text: Final script for the student's own video.
Learning outcome: Students direct a voice through character, emotion, and pacing, and compare two voice-over takes.

rows: Opening: Listen to two voices reading the same line; discuss the difference.
Teacher demo: Voice Card: character, emotion, speed, pauses.
Guided practice: Write a Voice Card for the sample script.
Creative production: Create a Voice Card for the own script; teacher generates two takes to compare.
Reflection & saving files: Choose the best take and save the audio file.

blocks.text: Learning outcome: Students split a script into 4–6 scenes, each with a visual world and an emotional meaning.

rows: Opening: Watch a short clip and count its scenes.
Teacher demo: How a storyboard plans scenes before any visuals are made.
Guided practice: Break the sample script into scenes together.
Creative production: Build a storyboard: dialogue, visual world, and feeling for every scene.
Reflection & saving files: Check that the story is simple enough to produce.

blocks.text: Learning outcome: Students write clear image prompts and keep characters and style consistent across scenes.

rows: Opening: Guess what prompt created a shown image.
Teacher demo: Prompt formula: subject, setting, lighting, composition, style.
Guided practice: Improve a weak prompt step by step.
Creative production: Create a Style Bible and prompts for every scene.
Reflection & saving files: Peer check: are the prompts clear and consistent?

blocks.text: Learning outcome: Students generate scene visuals, choose the best results, and revise prompts when output is off.

rows: Opening: Recap the Style Bible; safety check on topics and content.
Teacher demo: Teacher generates one scene live and explains choosing and rejecting results.
Guided practice: Revise one prompt together after a poor result.
Creative production: Generate and select the main image for each scene with teacher help.
Reflection & saving files: Rename and organise image files.

blocks.text: One selected visual for every scene.
Learning outcome: Students bring still images to life with motion, camera movement, and transitions between scenes.

rows: Opening: Compare a still image with the same image animated.
Teacher demo: Motion prompts, camera moves, and transition styles.
Guided practice: Animate one sample scene together.
Creative production: Create motion clips for the scenes with teacher help; check characters, text, and symbols first.
Reflection & saving files: Save clips and note which ones need revision.

blocks.text: Learning outcome: Students edit a vertical 9:16 video with the voice-over as the backbone, plus sound effects and subtitles.

rows: Opening: Watch a silent video, then the same video with sound.
Teacher demo: Canva basics: timeline, voice-over backbone, subtitles, ambience.
Guided practice: Import scenes and place the voice-over together.
Creative production: Edit the full video with subtitles and sound effects.
Reflection & saving files: Export a draft and save the project.

blocks.text: Learning outcome: Students give and use feedback with a simple rubric, and plan safe, honest sharing of their work.

rows: Opening: Quick review of rules from the AI Promise.
Teacher demo: Feedback rubric; how to write a thumbnail and caption; crediting AI help.
Guided practice: Review a sample video with the rubric.
Creative production: Revise the video from peer feedback; make a thumbnail and caption.
Reflection & saving files: Teacher checkpoint: subtitles, audio, AI credit, file name.

blocks.text: Learning outcome: Students present their video, explain their workflow and creative decisions, and reflect on responsible AI use.

rows: Opening: Set up the exhibition and rehearse the presentation.
Teacher demo: Presentation tips: workflow, tools, decisions, and ethics.
Guided practice: Practise a 1-minute explanation with a partner.
Creative production: Showcase videos to classmates, with parents where invited; explain the process.
Reflection & saving files: Reflection and certificate ceremony.
